+
+# number of top counted pairs kept in the "hot" candidate set during training
+_HOT_PAIRS = 64
+
+def _max_count_pairs(stats, hot):
+    """
+    Training helper: return (top, pairs) where top is max(stats.values()) and
+    pairs lists every pair whose count equals top (in no particular order).
+    hot = [set, T] caches all pairs with count >= T (a superset of them, stale
+    entries allowed), so most calls only look at a few dozen pairs instead of
+    every counted pair. Valid as long as counts never grow except for pairs
+    reported via _add_new_pairs; max() of an empty stats raises as usual.
+    """
+    pairs, T = hot
+    if pairs:
+        hp = list(pairs)
+        hv = list(map(stats.get, hp, repeat(0)))
+        top = max(hv)
+        if top >= T:
+            # every pair with count >= T is in hot, so all maxima are too
+            return top, list(compress(hp, map(top.__eq__, hv)))
+    # (re)build the hot set from the full counts
+    vals = list(stats.values())
+    top = max(vals)
+    if len(vals) > _HOT_PAIRS:
+        T = sorted(vals, reverse=True)[_HOT_PAIRS - 1]
+    else:
+        T = min(vals)
+    hot[0] = set(compress(stats, map(T.__le__, vals)))
+    hot[1] = T
+    return top, list(compress(stats, map(top.__eq__, vals)))
+
+def _add_new_pairs(stats, hot, idx):
+    """
+    After merging into the new token idx: the only pairs whose counts grew
+    are the brand new ones containing idx, which sit at the end of stats
+    (dict insertion order); add those reaching the hot threshold.
+    """
+    pairs, T = hot
+    for p in reversed(stats):
+        if idx not in p:
+            break
+        if stats[p] >= T:
+            pairs.add(p)
+
